source_evidence: src/Storages/TimeSeries/tryGetLiteralAlternatives.cpp: recognizes literal OR terms, rejects regex metacharacters such as character classes.
src/Storages/StorageTimeSeriesSelector.cpp::matcherToAST: if literal alternatives, builds in(tag,tuple(strings)); otherwise builds anchored match(tag,regex).
src/TableFunctions/TableFunctionTimeSeriesSelector.h: native selector table function accepts selectors and bounded samples read.
interpretation: Both syntaxes produce the same source-pinned labels/timestamps and numeric outputs. The observed 1.34% wall and 0.85% CPU differences are below 1.76% A/A drift; no speed advantage is established. EXPLAIN TimeSeriesSelector shows the same 6400-ID set and all 128/128 SAMPLES granules, explaining why the regex rewrite does not prune sample reads on this mixed-label layout. Compact form used about 1.08MB less peak per-query tracker memory, but single fixture/one job does not prove a general memory benefit.

limitations: One 32k one-sample high-churn fixture with branch in Map and no dedicated branch primary-key column. Not the real Grafana multi-branch stage query distribution.
One run on 4-vCPU GitHub-hosted runner; small effects are below observed control drift and no cross-runner precision is claimed.
EXPLAIN resolves 6400 candidate IDs and scans all SAMPLES granules; no structural pruning improvement observed. Parts/marks may differ at other densities.

The optimizer path is verified by pinned C++ source and semantically equivalent output. EXPLAIN does not expose original tag predicate at all operator depths; do not attribute 1.34% to a particular function.
